_readme: Hand-written copy for each project, in Ahmed's own voice. Overrides role / tagline / summary / highlights from the synced project.json files, so re-running `npm run sync` never undoes it. Leave a field out to fall back to the synced text.

yalla-kora.role: Frontend developer, with the mw3abee team
yalla-kora.tagline: A World Cup 2026 app for Arabic and Kurdish football fans
yalla-kora.summary: A phone-first football app that mobile operators offer to their subscribers: live scores, fixtures, match details, predictions and a short daily quiz. Most fans open it from a text message on a mobile connection, so I worked hard on keeping it fast and easy to read in Arabic and Kurdish.
highlights: Match pages split into simple tabs, so fans find events, stats and line-ups without scrolling forever
A daily quiz with a timer per question, built to be quick and fair to play on a phone
Arabic and Kurdish (Sorani) right-to-left layouts, light and dark themes, and a different look for each operator
A small Next.js server layer that keeps subscriber sessions private

snap-games.role: Frontend developer, with the mw3abee team
snap-games.tagline: Swipe through quick HTML5 games, earn points, keep a streak
snap-games.summary: A game app offered through mobile operators in Iraq and Nigeria. Players swipe through a feed of small games, play in one tap, and earn points toward levels. I worked on the feed, the game player and the progress screens, in Arabic, English and Kurdish.
highlights: A vertical feed that opens each game in a safe, sandboxed frame, with full screen and a prompt to rotate the phone
Levels and daily streaks that give players a reason to come back
The right language and reading direction from the very first screen

3abee.role: Frontend developer, with the mw3abee team
3abee.tagline: One storefront for gift cards and game credit, branded for four operators
3abee.summary: A store where subscribers buy gift cards, game credit and subscriptions and pay through their phone provider. The same app is branded for Sudani, Syriatel, Chinguitel and STORE 70 in Senegal, each with its own colours, languages and currency.
highlights: Four brands from one codebase, chosen when the app is built
Arabic, English and French, with Sudanese, Syrian, Mauritanian and West African currencies
Topping up a game account directly with a player ID, as well as buying cards
A test suite that keeps the four brands from breaking each other

lumio.role: Mobile developer, with the Media World team
lumio.tagline: A kids' streaming app in Arabic: shows, short clips and characters to collect
lumio.summary: A streaming app for Arabic-speaking children aged about three to eight, with a separate area for parents behind a PIN. I built it in React Native from the team's design system, right-to-left from the start, and made sure progress isn't lost on a weak connection.
highlights: Shows organised by season, plus a short-clip feed sized for small hands
Watching every day unlocks characters children can collect
Playback position is saved on the device and synced later, so nothing is lost offline
All colours and sizes come from the design system's tokens, so screens stay consistent

first-step.tagline: The staff portal for a football, padel and tennis academy in Amman
first-step.summary: The tool the staff at First Step Academy use every day to book fields, see what's free and keep track of payments and expenses. It's all in Arabic, and I tried to make the booking flow quick enough to use while someone is waiting at the desk.
highlights: A step-by-step booking flow with availability for each field and half-hour slots
A shared timeline for the tennis courts showing how busy each slot is
Simple reports for the owner: income, busy hours, unpaid bookings and expenses
Runs on Cloudflare with a small database, so it's cheap for the academy to keep online

first-step-customer.tagline: Lets players check a free field and send a booking request
first-step-customer.summary: The public side of the First Step academy. Players choose a sport, a date and a time, see what's available, and send a request the staff can accept from their portal. They can also look up their bookings with their name and phone number.
highlights: Three short steps from choosing a time to sending the request on WhatsApp
Shows availability across football, padel and tennis in one place
Requests go straight to the staff portal's inbox

first-step-mobile.tagline: A phone app so the academy staff can book and check the day on the go
first-step-mobile.summary: A React Native companion to the First Step staff portal, for staff who are out on the fields rather than at the desk. It covers today's schedule, a booking flow, the bookings list and a monthly finances view, all in Arabic.
highlights: The same booking steps as the web portal, adapted for one hand
Today's and this month's income at a glance
Works against the live portal, or with sample data for training new staff

tennis-booking.tagline: A booking portal for a tennis club, built around one shared court timeline
tennis-booking.summary: An adaptation of the First Step portal for a club with four tennis courts. Staff see in one view how many courts are taken in every half hour, then pick a free court for the player.
highlights: One timeline for all four courts instead of four separate calendars
Shows which courts and durations are still free for the chosen time
Its own deployment and database, so it runs separately from the academy

kinetiq.tagline: An offline-first app for Pilates studios, CrossFit boxes, dojos and gyms
kinetiq.summary: A side project exploring what one app could look like for very different kinds of gyms. It has screens for the gym owner, coaches, the front desk and members, and keeps working when the gym's internet doesn't.
highlights: Separate screens for owners, coaches, front desk, a TV display and members
Small touches for each kind of gym: reformer spots for Pilates, workout boards for CrossFit, belt progress for martial arts
Everything is stored in the browser and synced later, so classes can still be checked in offline
Feature switches so a gym only sees what it needs

ims.tagline: Inventory for hospital labs that tracks every lot and expiry date
ims.summary: An inventory system for laboratory staff, who need to know what's on the shelf, what expires soon and what to order next. It suggests which lot to use first, explains its reorder suggestions, and works in both English and Arabic.
highlights: Suggests the lot that expires first, and asks for a reason when someone chooses another
Reorder levels based on what the lab actually used, with the working shown on screen
Approvals for sensitive actions such as disposing of stock
A simpler layout for storekeepers on handheld scanners, in English and Arabic

roost.tagline: A phone app that helps home daycare providers log the day and update parents
roost.summary: Home daycare providers have their hands full, so logging a nap or a meal takes two taps, and parents get a daily report automatically. The app keeps working without internet and syncs when it can.
highlights: Quick logging for meals, naps, nappies, incidents and medication
A daily report page for parents, sent automatically
Attendance, drills and documents gathered into one record ready for inspections
Works offline first, with careful syncing so no entry is lost

hax-oi.role: Web development, with the HAX team
hax-oi.tagline: A pilot site that helps experienced executives find where their skills fit
hax-oi.summary: A website for a small advisory service in the Gulf. Visitors read about the service and fill in a short review of their experience, and the team uses it to prepare tailored opportunity notes. We were careful with personal data and kept the wording within what the client had approved.
highlights: A short multi-step review that tells people honestly whether the service fits them
Opportunity notes that keep facts, interpretation and unknowns clearly apart
Privacy-minded analytics that strip personal details before anything is sent

shopraha-dashboard.role: Frontend developer in the ShopRaha team
shopraha-dashboard.tagline: The back-office for an online grocery in Kuwait
shopraha-dashboard.summary: The admin tool ShopRaha's operations, content and customer care staff used every day, built on top of the open-source Saleor dashboard. With the team, I worked on the parts specific to a grocery business: recipes, delivery slots, deals and customer wallets.
highlights: A recipes section where each ingredient links to a product customers can add to their basket
Delivery time slots and return pickups for the operations team
Deals such as buy-one-get-one, bundles and wallet cashback for the marketing team
Grocery details like price per kilo and units of measure

cockpit.tagline: An operations dashboard for orders, catalogue, marketing and deliveries
cockpit.summary: An internal dashboard for ShopRaha's operations team, connected to both the shop's GraphQL API and the delivery service. I mostly worked on the catalogue, marketing campaigns, customers and the main dashboard, alongside teammates who built the delivery tools.
highlights: A route planner where dispatchers drag deliveries into routes on a map
Delivery zones drawn on the map, with capacity for each time slot
Banners, cashback, vouchers and featured products, in English and Arabic

btr-smooth.tagline: A portal where online shops manage their orders, stock and deliveries
btr-smooth.summary: Smooth let other online shops in Kuwait store their products in the BTR warehouse and have them delivered. Merchants use this portal to follow orders, send in stock, see reports and top up their account. It lives in a shared monorepo with the other internal tools.
highlights: One timeline per order, from the warehouse shelf to the customer's door
Reports merchants can download for their own records
API hooks generated from the backend's schema, so the frontend stays in step with it

btr-rover.tagline: A dispatch dashboard for planning routes and driver schedules
btr-rover.summary: The tool dispatchers use to plan delivery routes, manage drivers and vehicles, and set how many deliveries each hour can take. I contributed to parts of it alongside the team that built it.
highlights: Route planning from unassigned orders on a map
A weekly schedule grid for drivers' shifts
An hourly view of delivery load against capacity

btr-halo.role: Built by my teammates; I worked on shared packages in the same monorepo
btr-halo.tagline: Warehouse management: receiving, stock and picking
btr-halo.summary: The warehouse system used in ShopRaha's fulfilment centres for receiving stock, putting it away and picking orders. My teammates built this app; it's shown here because it shares the monorepo and packages I worked on.
highlights: Receiving with barcode, quantity and expiry for each line
A visual editor for laying out aisles and racks
Support for several warehouses and several merchants

shopraha-app.role: Built by my teammates at ShopRaha
shopraha-app.tagline: ShopRaha's grocery app for iPhone, Android and web
shopraha-app.summary: The customer app for ShopRaha, an online grocery in Kuwait. My teammates built this app; it's shown here because it ran on the backend, dashboards and services I worked on with them.
highlights: Browse aisles, search in Arabic or English and fill a basket
Choose a delivery slot and pay by KNET, card or cash
Follow the order until it arrives

shopraha-web.role: Built by my teammates at ShopRaha
shopraha-web.tagline: ShopRaha's web shop and the page that launched its app
shopraha-web.summary: The ShopRaha web store from 2021–22 and the landing page for the app launch, built by the team before and around my time there. It's included to show the whole product the dashboards served.
highlights: Aisle pages, product pages and a slide-in basket
Checkout with saved addresses and delivery slots
Arabic by default, with English

aod.tagline: An Android experiment: a ring of light around the camera while the phone sleeps
aod.summary: A small Android app I made for fun. While the screen is off, it draws a soft ring of light around the front camera, with different light patterns and colours for notifications. Since the app itself can't run in a browser, the demo is a web simulator that uses the same drawing code.
highlights: Twelve light patterns, from a slow breath to a charging ring
Each app's notification can tint the ring with its own colour
A calibration screen, because phones don't always report where the camera really is
Kept gentle on the battery: a capped frame rate and a slight drift to protect the screen

aiwin.tagline: Website and product catalogue for a Jordanian waterproofing manufacturer
aiwin.summary: A new website for AIWIN, a Jordanian maker of bitumen waterproofing and insulation products, moved from an old WordPress site to a fast static site. Engineers and contractors can find each product and download its technical data sheet.
highlights: A page for every product, with photos and a downloadable data sheet
All the content in one place, so it's easy for the client to update
Static, so it loads quickly and costs little to host

soho-cafe.tagline: A QR menu for a hotel restaurant, café and lounge in Amman
soho-cafe.summary: A digital menu for SOHO Midtown Hotel in Amman. Guests scan a QR code at their table and see the current menu, which comes straight from the hotel's point-of-sale system, so the staff don't have to update it twice.
highlights: Separate menus for the restaurant, lobby, room service and minibar
Search in English and Arabic
Reads the hotel's POS system, hiding staff-only items

heartfeltcode.tagline: A simple site for my small consultancy for non-technical founders
heartfeltcode.summary: The website for Heartfelt Code, where I help early-stage founders without a technical co-founder turn an idea into a working product. I kept it light: a static site with almost no JavaScript, a few case studies, and a contact form.
highlights: Fast and simple, with almost no JavaScript
Case studies written as problem, what we built, and what happened
Light and dark themes with readable contrast

drift-academy.tagline: An Arabic landing page for a drift driving school in Jordan
drift-academy.summary: A one-page site for Raafat Haroun's drift academy, written in Jordanian Arabic, presenting the courses, the coach and a booking form.

augment-clone.tagline: Practice: rebuilding an existing landing page to learn its layout
augment-clone.summary: A practice exercise where I rebuilt the layout of augment.org's landing page in Next.js and Tailwind to learn from its design. The design and most of the text belong to the original site.

eliteshop.tagline: A practice storefront with a catalogue, filters, cart and checkout
eliteshop.summary: A storefront I built to practise animation and state management: a home page with deals, a filterable catalogue, a wishlist and a cart drawer. The demo adds sample products and a pretend checkout so it can be clicked through.
highlights: Catalogue search with category, price and sort filters
Cart and wishlist that survive a page reload
Light and dark themes

gym-pwa.tagline: An early experiment: a gym member app that installs on the phone
gym-pwa.summary: An early experiment with progressive web apps: gym members can check their membership, browse exercises and log their sets, and install it on their phone like an app.
highlights: A simple workout logger for sets, reps and weights
Installs on the phone and opens offline

saas-starter.tagline: A starting point for multi-team SaaS apps: sign-in, teams and billing
saas-starter.summary: A starting point I set up for software-as-a-service apps, with sign-in, organisations, roles and billing models. It is mostly scaffolding; the demo adds a few sample pages so the layout can be explored.
highlights: Organisations with owner, admin and member roles
A dashboard layout that works on phones and desktops

sports-booking.tagline: An early prototype for booking football pitches and padel courts
sports-booking.summary: An early React Native prototype for booking a football pitch, a padel court or a hall at one sports centre, in Arabic and English.
highlights: A four-step booking flow: place, date, time and payment
Arabic and English with a language switch
